lead.t: Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis is most often the first manifestation of APS-1, followed by hypoparathyroidism and then by Addison disease, which typically develops in early adolescence.

snip.t: Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis: Associated with T cell defects, including Job syndrome (an inherited condition with a defect in Th17 T cell responses).

qs.q: A patient with chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis has a genetic defect impairing Th17 cell differentiation. Why are these patients specifically susceptible to superficial Candida infections?
o: They lack mucosal secretory antibody responses
They cannot produce interferon for macrophages
They fail to recruit adequate tissue neutrophils
They suffer from impaired complement activation
qs.e: Th17 cells secrete IL-17, which is crucial for inducing epithelial antimicrobial peptides and recruiting neutrophils to mucosal surfaces.
